newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money off highs, guilder firms a touch.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money off highs, guilder firms a touch.

text.p: Overnight guilders came off their highs late Wednesday, but dealers said this reflected an uneven distribution among market particpants rather than a major overall increase in market liquidity.

"A lot of early deals were done at 2.81 percent but later in the day, some players were offering," one dealer said. "There was little demand by then, so rates had to come down quite sharply." As a result, call money ended sharply lower at 2.38 percent bid.
Dealers said trade had focused almost exclusively on overnight guilders.
They said some money had flowed back into the market through the repurchase of Dutch Treasury Certificates by the finance ministry's agent.
Overnight guilders were unlikely to scale recent peaks again on Thursday before the expiry of the current special advances pact, some said.
The guilder was slightly firmer against the mark, fixing at 112.18 per 100 marks from 112.22 on Tuesday.
